name: Elizabeth Campos
life: “I still remember cutting a sample cake into eleven sensible pieces.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Elizabeth by a small Monday habit. Elizabeth checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I make fancy cakes. I delivered one small enough to share without pretending it was a feast.
appearance: Elizabeth has a dark undercut with a longer wave on top, a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, and a favorite piece of clothing, a washed violet jersey. It usually goes with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. When somebody else has the floor, Elizabeth gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Elizabeth takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To deliver a genuinely shareable small cake.
family: Rosa Vance is Elizabeth’s cousin raised in the same household. Elizabeth offers the first invitation. Rosa gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The skipper goes ashore*, Rosa says, “I have always been seasick. I told the skipper which bench has the best steady horizon for talking after a trip.”
connections: Barbara Jackson. Both tips and an affordable birthday cake depend on the dessert table being welcomed.
